title: IPTV workshop: from zero to a video player
summary: 10 steps to a complete local video-on-demand project. Prerequisites: JavaScript, React and Next.js basics.

lessons.title: Set up the video project

explanation.text: Build a video catalog with a television-style interface. Start with videos you created or can distribute. This project uses Next.js App Router with TypeScript and no src directory. The first stages produce video on demand; a real live channel additionally needs a live input and a continuously running encoder.

codeExample.code:
npx create-next-app@latest video-school --ts --app --no-src-dir --use-npm
cd video-school
npm install hls.js
npm run dev

exercise.task: Create the project, then open localhost:3000. Find app/page.tsx and app/layout.tsx.
hints: The starter page appears. Stop the server with Ctrl+C when you need to change directories.

lessons.title: Model the channels

explanation.text: Each channel has a stable ID, a name and a playlist address. The player uses an allowed catalog address rather than an arbitrary visitor-supplied URL. Create lib at the project root. The next step generates the stream path.

lessons.title: Create your first HLS playlist

explanation.text: Install FFmpeg from its official site and check ffmpeg -version. Create public/streams/demo, then run the command from video-school. It generates a 30-second test pattern with a test tone and segments it. HLS uses a .m3u8 playlist referencing .ts segments. The browser must load both.

codeExample.code: ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360:rate=25 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000 -t 30 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 100 -sc_threshold 0 -c:a aac -f hls -hls_time 4 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_segment_filename public/streams/demo/segment%03d.ts public/streams/demo/index.m3u8

exercise.task: Generate the files, then open /streams/demo/index.m3u8. Check that one referenced segment also responds.
hints: The playlist begins with #EXTM3U and ends with #EXT-X-ENDLIST. This is finished content, not a live broadcast.
exercise.solution:
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc=size=640x360:rate=25 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000 -t 30 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -g 100 -sc_threshold 0 -c:a aac -f hls -hls_time 4 -hls_playlist_type vod -hls_segment_filename public/streams/demo/segment%03d.ts public/streams/demo/index.m3u8

The playlist begins with #EXTM3U and ends with #EXT-X-ENDLIST. This is finished content, not a live broadcast.

lessons.title: Serve the catalog through an API
lessons.concept: Serve the catalog through an API

explanation.text: A Route Handler returns JSON. The optional id parameter selects one item: no id returns the catalog; an unknown ID returns 404. These videos are public and need no sign-in. A paid service would need server-side session and playback-entitlement checks.

exercise.task: Test /api/channels, ?id=demo and ?id=unknown in the Network tab.
hints: The statuses are 200, 200 and 404. The last response never silently returns a different channel.

quiz.question: Which status for an unknown ID?
quiz.explanation: The statuses are 200, 200 and 404. The last response never silently returns a different channel.

lessons.title: Build the HLS player

explanation.text: The player is a client component because it controls a video element. Use native HLS when available, otherwise hls.js. Clean up the instance when the source changes. Controls let the viewer start playback manually; do not assume audible autoplay is allowed.

exercise.task: Create components/Player.tsx. Identify the cleanup function and the error message.
hints: The component compiles. The next step displays it. Changing src destroys the old instance.

quiz.explanation: The component compiles. The next step displays it. Changing src destroys the old instance.

explanation.text: The server imports the catalog and passes data to the client player. The page stays simple: a heading, a channel name and a player. You now have an end-to-end project: media files → playlist → player. Keep this working before adding interactions.

lessons.title: Save a favorite channel

explanation.text: localStorage remembers a preference in this browser without creating an account. Read it in an effect and surface storage failures. Do not write the initial value before reading or you can erase a saved favorite. Import Favorite in app/page.tsx, then place <Favorite id={channel.id} /> below each channel heading.

lessons.title: Add a program guide

explanation.text: A program guide contains start and end times independently of the player. Store dates with explicit time zones and use an exclusive end: at 10:30, a program ending at 10:30 is no longer current. This demonstration schedule does not turn on-demand video into a live channel.

hints: The results are none, Demo program, Demo program, none. The phone time zone does not change the instant.

quiz.question: At its exact end time, is the program still current?
quiz.explanation: The results are none, Demo program, Demo program, none. The phone time zone does not change the instant.

summary: The results are none, Demo program, Demo program, none. The phone time zone does not change the instant.

lessons.title: Test playback and failures

explanation.text: Automate HTTP contract checks and test actual playback in a browser. A 200 response does not prove that picture or sound works. Run npm run dev in one terminal and node scripts/check.mjs in another. To test a failure, temporarily rename a segment and reload the player, then restore it.

exercise.task: Run the test, then verify Play/Pause, sound, favorites and no overflow at 360px.
hints: The script passes when files exist. A missing playlist or segment makes it fail.

quiz.question: What does this script prove?
quiz.explanation: The script passes when files exist. A missing playlist or segment makes it fail.

summary: The script passes when files exist. A missing playlist or segment makes it fail.

lessons.title: Ship the project and plan live streaming
lessons.concept: Ship the project and plan live streaming

explanation.text: Stop the dev server before starting production on the same port. This demo keeps small videos in public. For a large library, encode outside the web server and use media storage/CDN. For live delivery, replace the test pattern with a live input and keep FFmpeg running on a dedicated machine; short-lived function hosting is unsuitable for this encoder.

codeExample.code:
npm run build
npm run start
# In a second terminal:
node scripts/check.mjs

exercise.task: Validate production and write a review: files created, passing test, fixed error and next improvement. If media moves to another domain, verify HTTPS and CORS for playlists and segments.
hints: The final project plays your video, exposes a catalog, remembers a favorite and displays a demo guide. Live broadcasting and subscriptions remain extensions to implement.
exercise.solution:
npm run build
npm run start
# In a second terminal:
node scripts/check.mjs
